Neeps and Tatties

Served at: Burns Night Supper

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Neeps and tatties is a traditional Scottish dish consisting of mashed turnips (neeps) and potatoes (tatties). It is a staple side dish served at Burns Night Supper, a celebration honoring the poet Robert Burns, and often accompanies haggis, the evening's centerpiece.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (900 g) rutabagas (neeps), peeled and chopped
  • 2 pounds (900 g) potatoes (tatties), peeled and chopped
  • 4 tablespoons (60 g) unsalted butter
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) whole milk or cream
  • Salt, to taste
  • Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • Chopped fresh parsley or chives, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. Place the chopped rutabagas in a large pot and cover with cold water.
  2. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 20-25 minutes until tender.
  3. Drain the rutabagas and return them to the pot.
  4. In a separate pot, place the chopped potatoes and cover with cold water.
  5. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 15-20 minutes until tender.
  6. Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot.
  7. Mash the rutabagas with 2 tablespoons of butter, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
  8. Mash the potatoes with the remaining butter and milk or cream, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
  9. Serve the neeps and tatties side by side or layered on a plate, garnished with chopped parsley or chives if desired.

Tips

  • For a creamier texture, add more butter or cream to the mash.
  • Use yellow-fleshed potatoes for a richer flavor.
  • Serve immediately for the best taste and texture.
